settings.display.theme.title: Theme
settings.display.theme.hint: “System” follows your device's light or dark mode.
settings.display.wallpaperAccent.title: Accent colour from your wallpaper
settings.display.wallpaperAccent.hint: Uses the accent colour Android takes from your wallpaper. The rest of the app stays as it is.
settings.display.cards.title: Trip cards on the home page
settings.display.cards.hint: Default size for every trip. “Auto”: upcoming trips large, past trips compact. You can override this per trip in the ⋯ menu on its card.
settings.display.navBar.title: Navigation bar
settings.display.navBar.hint: The bar at the bottom with Trips, {travellers} and Settings. “Automatic” slides it away as soon as you open a trip, including the timeline, the route planner and the share screen; the arrow at the top left of the map brings you back. “Always” keeps it on screen everywhere.
settings.display.mapStyle.title: Map style
settings.display.mapStyle.hint: Applies to every map on this device.
settings.photoCache.title: Photo cache
settings.photoCache.help: Photos you look at are kept, so you can see them again without internet. Without a limit that grows to hundreds of megabytes on a busy account; once the cache reaches the limit, the photos you haven't looked at for longest go first.
settings.photoCache.clearConfirm.title: Clear the cache?
settings.photoCache.clearConfirm.body: Saved photos are cleared. They're fetched again as soon as you're online. Nothing from your trips is lost.
settings.backup.title: Backup
settings.backup.help: One file with all your trips, stops, route points and notes, plus your settings. Photos are in it as references, not as files: they're already in your gallery or on your Immich server.
settings.backup.intro: Puts everything in one file {where}, then opens the share sheet so you can put it somewhere safe right away. Restoring adds what you don't have yet and leaves existing trips alone.
settings.backup.restoreConfirm.title: Restore backup?
settings.backup.restoreConfirm.body_one: This backup is from {date} and holds {count} trip. Trips you already have stay as they are; the rest is added.
settings.backup.restoreConfirm.body_othe: This backup is from {date} and holds {count} trips. Trips you already have stay as they are; the rest is added.
settings.backup.restored.coversLost: covers come back once your photos are linked
settings.backup.restored.summary: {parts}. Reload the app to see everything.
settings.backup.error.unreadable: This isn't a readable backup file.
settings.backup.error.newer: This backup is from a newer version of the app.
settings.local.title: Without a server
settings.local.card.stored: All your trips, points and notes are on this device. Nothing leaves it, and you don't need an account.
settings.local.card.needsServer: Travel companions, share links and automatic backups do need a server. If you connect one later, everything here is uploaded in one go.
settings.local.sheet.intro: Everything stays on your device. No account, no server, nothing leaves it.
settings.local.works.tracking.title: Route tracking
settings.local.works.tracking: Your location is kept on your device, even without internet. The tracker runs entirely on your phone.
settings.local.works.plan.title: Planning trips
settings.local.works.plan: Stops, nights, transport, flights and day trips. Everything adds up as usual.
settings.local.works.photos.title: Photos from your gallery
settings.local.works.photos: Photos on your device are linked to a trip by date and put on the map using their GPS.
settings.local.works.maps.title: Map, globe and timeline
settings.local.works.maps: The maps and the globe get their tiles straight from OpenStreetMap. No account needed.
settings.local.needs.companions.title: Travel companions
settings.local.needs.companions: Working on one trip together and seeing each other's live position. That takes two devices that can find each other somewhere.
settings.local.needs.shareLinks.title: Share links
settings.local.needs.shareLinks: Instead, you put a trip in one file and send it on yourself.
settings.local.needs.backup.title: Automatic backup
settings.local.needs.backup: Everything is on your device. Make a backup now and then in Settings.
settings.local.needs.immich: If you already keep your photos on your own Immich server, you can connect it later.
settings.local.later.title: Want a server later?
settings.local.later.intro: A server is just a computer that's always on. An old laptop with Linux and Docker works fine; so does a Raspberry Pi or a NAS.
settings.local.later.step1: Install Docker on that machine and get the code:
settings.local.later.step2: In that folder, run ./install.sh. It asks for the address you want to reach the app on, then sets everything up by itself.
settings.local.later.step3: Create an account at that address. From then on you can invite people too.
settings.local.later.step4: In the app, go to, choose Connect a server and enter that address.
settings.local.later.outro: Your trips come along in one go. You don't have to enter anything again, and you can go back too: disconnecting a server leaves everything on your device.
settings.airports.title: Default airports
settings.airports.help: Tap an airport to make it your default: that's the airport already filled in as the departure on a new flight. Add as many as you like.
settings.airports.hint: Your home airports, for filling in flights.
settings.notify.title: Notifications on your phone
settings.notify.help: Your device has no Google push service, so nothing can be sent to the app. Instead the app checks for itself: every quarter of an hour it asks whether there's anything for you. So a notification can arrive up to fifteen minutes later than intended.
settings.notify.toggleHint: Access requests and invitations arrive as notifications, even when the app is closed.
settings.notify.on: On. You'll hear about a new message within a quarter of an hour.
settings.notify.denied: Your phone doesn't allow notifications for this app. Turn them on in your device's app settings.
settings.notify.failed: Couldn't turn it on. Try again in a moment.
settings.globe.title: Globe
settings.globe.help: Every stop from your route planner gets a dot on the globe. For the trip that's highlighted at that moment, that always happens. With “Always”, every other trip shows its stops too.
settings.globe.hint: Stops along the way on the home page globe.
settings.selfLocation.title: Your location
settings.selfLocation.help: Your position comes from route tracking, so you only see yourself while you're tracking a trip. The app never asks for your location separately.
settings.selfLocation.hint: On a trip's map you always see yourself while tracking.
settings.selfLocation.homeHint: Also shows your position as a dot on the globe.
settings.tracking.title: Route tracking
settings.tracking.help: Every interval the app switches the GPS on briefly for exactly one position, then off again; in between, tracking costs nothing. If you stay in the same place, those readings are merged into one point instead of a tangle of dots. So a longer interval saves a lot of battery. Offline, everything is buffered and uploaded later. Needs location set to “{always}”.
settings.tracking.hint: Records your route during a trip, even with the screen off.
settings.tracking.stopConfirm.title: Stop tracking?
settings.tracking.stopConfirm.body: The route of "{title}" is no longer recorded. What was already recorded stays.
settings.tracking.waitingFix: Waiting for the first GPS fix…
settings.tracking.noTrips: No current or upcoming trips. Create one first.
settings.tracking.lastFix.label: last fix
settings.tracking.log.title: Location log
settings.about.tagline: Self-hosted travel tracker on top of your own Immich server. Open source (AGPL-3.0).
settings.update.upToDate: You're up to date. Build {build} is the latest.
settings.update.permission: Turn on "Install unknown apps" and press again.
settings.update.banner.title: New version available
settings.update.banner.fakeInstall: Test notice, there's nothing to install.
settings.dev.screens.title: Preview screens
settings.dev.screens.help: The real screens, not a copy: this is what a new user sees. A preview changes nothing in your own app, so open it as often as you like: the tour isn't marked as “seen”, your name isn't saved, and “Start without a server” does nothing on the sign-in screen.
settings.dev.invite.title: Preview notices
settings.dev.invite.hint: Opens a small menu to choose how many trips it lists and whether they have a photo.
settings.dev.invite.sheetHint: Shows the real notice. Nothing changes on your account, and closing it takes you nowhere.
settings.dev.invite.note: With photos, it borrows the covers of your own trips: a made-up photo doesn't exist and would only show up as a broken frame.
settings.dev.covers.title: Covers without a photo
settings.dev.covers.hint: Every trip without photos gets its own colour and an icon that follows from its name.
settings.dev.inbox.title: Notification list
settings.dev.inbox.hint: Opens the bell on the travellers page with a request, an invitation, an approval and a rejection in it. Replies go nowhere.
settings.dev.updateBanner.title: Update notice
settings.dev.updateBanner.hint: Shows the bar as if a new version is ready. Install does nothing.
settings.dev.mode.title: Developer mode
settings.dev.mode.hint: Hides this tab again. You get it back through the version at the bottom of “About”.
settings.profile.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other sessions were signed out, please sign in again.
settings.profile.photo.title: Profile photo
settings.profile.photo.hint: What travel companions see of you on maps and in timelines.
settings.profile.name.title: Name and username
settings.profile.name.name: Name
settings.profile.name.usernameHint: Friends use this to add you to trips
settings.profile.password.title: Password
settings.profile.password.hint: At least ten characters. You stay signed in on your other devices.
settings.server.title: Server
settings.server.help: The address your MarkMySteps runs on. If you change it, you're signed out and sign in again on the new server.
settings.server.hint: The server this session talks to.
settings.server.invalid: That's not a valid address. Start with https:// and add a domain.
settings.server.https: Use https, otherwise your password travels unencrypted.
settings.server.confirm.title: Use a different server?
settings.server.confirm.body: The app will then talk to {origin}. You'll be signed out and need to sign in again there. Trips that are only on the old server stay there.
settings.immich.connected: Connected to Immich. API key checked and stored encrypted.
settings.immich.help.what: Immich is a free, open-source photo library you run yourself: your own Google Photos, but on your own server. If you don't have one, you don't need to fill in anything here. MarkMySteps then uses your device's gallery.
settings.immich.help.stored: If you do connect it, your photos stay there. MarkMySteps only keeps references: the asset ID, the time and the GPS from the EXIF. Your API key goes into the database encrypted.
settings.immich.key.label: API key
settings.immich.key.help: A key that lets MarkMySteps into Immich on your behalf, so your password never ends up here. Once saved it can't be read back, only replaced. If you revoke it in Immich, the connection stops working straight away.
settings.immich.key.replace: Enter a new key to replace it
settings.immich.public.label: Public URL (optional)
settings.immich.public.help: Only for the “Open in Immich” button. The address above may be an internal address on your own network; this is the address you open Immich on yourself.
settings.accounts.pending.hint: These people signed up on your server. Until you let them in they can't do anything: their session is refused everywhere.
settings.accounts.created: Account @{username} created. Pass on the temporary password: {password}
settings.accounts.rejectConfirm.title: Decline {name}'s request?
settings.accounts.rejectConfirm.body: They won't be able to sign in. The account stays, so the same name and email can't be used again straight away.
settings.accounts.approved: {name} has been let in. They'll hear about it the next time their app checks.
settings.accounts.resetPrompt: New temporary password for @{username} (at least 10 characters):
settings.accounts.resetDone: Password for @{username} reset. All sessions signed out.
settings.accounts.removeConfirm.title: Delete account?
settings.accounts.removeConfirm.body: Account @{username} will be deleted, along with their own trips and routes.
settings.accounts.create.title: Create account
settings.accounts.create.hint: Create an account for a travel companion with a temporary password. They choose their own the first time they sign in.
settings.accounts.list.help: Anyone who signs up goes into a queue first: they can't do anything until you let the request in. An account you create here is approved straight away. They choose their own password when they first sign in; they can skip that, but then they keep seeing a reminder.
settings.accounts.list.hint: Everyone with an account on this server.
settings.accounts.list.empty: No account found with that name.
settings.polarsteps.title: Import from Polarsteps
settings.polarsteps.hint: Request your export at <path>polarsteps.com</path> and upload the zip here. Every trip in the export is created with its full GPS route.
settings.trackFiles.title: Route files
settings.trackFiles.hint: Export a trip as GPX or KML, or add a track you recorded somewhere else. Points outside the trip dates are skipped: they belong to another trip.
settings.offlineMap.title: Save map offline
settings.offlineMap.saved: {size} saved. This trip's map now works without internet.
settings.offlineMap.ready: Saves the map of the area you've been to, so it works without internet too.
settings.offlineMap.empty: Once this trip has a route or stops with a location, the area can be saved.
settings.offlineMap.satellite: The satellite map can't be saved offline. Choose another map style.
settings.password.tip.common: This is on every list an attacker tries first.
settings.password.tip.personal: Having your name, username or email in it makes it easy to guess.
settings.password.tip.longer: Longer helps more than complicated: try a sentence.
settings.password.tip.mix: Mix in capitals, numbers or punctuation.
settings.immich.title: Immich
settings.accounts.twoFactorConfirm.title: Reset 2FA?
settings.accounts.twoFactorConfirm.body: @{username} can then sign in again with just a password and is signed out everywhere. Only do this if they have lost both their phone and their recovery codes, and you are sure you are dealing with that person.
settings.accounts.twoFactorDone: 2FA for @{username} is off. All sessions are signed out.
settings.twoFactor.title: Two-step verification
settings.twoFactor.onHint: When you sign in, we ask for a code from your authenticator app as well as your password. If you lose your phone, you get in with a recovery code.
settings.twoFactor.offHint: A stolen or guessed password is then not enough: whoever signs in also needs the code from your authenticator app, such as Proton Authenticator.
settings.twoFactor.passwordFirst: Your password first, to show it is you and not someone holding your phone.
settings.twoFactor.step1: Open your authenticator app and choose to add a new account.
settings.twoFactor.step2: Scan this QR code, or type in the key below it.
settings.twoFactor.step3: Enter the code the app shows below.
settings.twoFactor.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
settings.twoFactor.typeKey: Scanning doesn't work? Type in this key:
settings.twoFactor.saveCodes: Save these recovery codes now. You only see them once. Each code works once and gets you in if you lose your phone. Keep them somewhere other than that phone, for example in your password manager.
settings.twoFactor.disableHint: Turning it off asks for your password and a code, so an open session is not enough.
settings.twoFactor.renewHint: The old recovery codes stop working after this. It asks for your password and a code.
settings.twoFactor.codeOrRecovery: Code from the app, or a recovery code
